ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The main body in the figure is an organic structure. After ignoring the curved arrows, the right side can be regarded as an ethoxy ester fragment: CH3CH2O-C(=O)-. This ester carbonyl carbon is connected leftward to a carbon chain, which continues to connect to a carbon bearing a methyl branch; this terminal carbon forms a double bond with an oxygen bearing hydrogen and a positive charge, namely C(C)=[OH+]. Reasoning: Write the SMILES according to connectivity; starting from the ethyl group on the right can be written as CCO, then adding the ester carbonyl as C(=O), then adding the two carbons on the left as CC, adding a methyl branch (C) on the terminal carbon, and finally writing the protonated oxonium double bond as =[OH+]. Therefore the SMILES is CCOC(=O)CC(C)=[OH+].

method.method_draft: First describe the image contents rather than the arrows: the right side is an ethoxy ester fragment CH3CH2O-C(=O)-, the carbonyl carbon is bonded to a carbon chain that continues to C(C)=[OH+], where the left carbon also has a methyl branch and the oxygen bears H and positive charge. Convert this connectivity into SMILES by starting at the ethyl group as CCO, writing the ester carbonyl as C(=O), continuing to the adjacent carbon chain as CC, adding the methyl branch on the terminal carbon as (C), and encoding the protonated oxonium double bond as =[OH+], yielding CCOC(=O)CC(C)=[OH+].
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中主体是一个有机结构，忽略弯箭头后，右侧可以看作乙氧基酯片段：CH3CH2O-C(=O)-。该酯羰基碳向左连接到一个碳链，继续连接到一个带甲基支链的碳；该末端碳与带氢且带正电荷的氧形成双键，即 C(C)=[OH+]。推理：按连通性写 SMILES，可从右侧乙基开始写为 CCO，接酯羰基为 C(=O)，再接左侧两个碳为 CC，在末端碳上加入甲基支链 (C)，最后写质子化氧鎓双键 =[OH+]。因此 SMILES 为 CCOC(=O)CC(C)=[OH+]。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription is the only genuinely distinct route for this image-grounded problem; it reads the drawn connectivity and converts it into a valid charged SMILES while ignoring the mechanism arrows.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the skeletal drawing: ignore the curved arrows; identify an ethyl ester on the right, O=C-O-CH2-CH3, attached through the carbonyl carbon to an alpha carbon chain leading left to a carbon bearing a methyl group and a protonated hydroxy/oxonium group shown as [OH+] double-bonded to that carbon.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the prompt instruction that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored, so only atom connectivity, bond orders, and formal charge from the drawn structure matter.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard skeletal-structure conventions: unlabeled vertices are carbons with implicit hydrogens, line ends are methyl groups, explicit O and H labels must be retained, a circled plus on oxygen gives [OH+], and double bonds/branching must be encoded in SMILES. Choose any equivalent valid SMILES, e.g. traverse from the ethyl group through the ester carbonyl into the carbon chain.
